没有 RoPE 时，注意力会随着键数量增长而变得平坦。SSMax 将每个 query 乘以
是从 1 开始的位置，因此 softmax 会随着上下文增长而变得更锐利。
带逐头 Q/K 归一化的 GQA。
48 个 query 头，8 个 KV 头，头维度 128。Q 和 K 在 RoPE 或 SSMax 之前按头进行 RMS 归一化。
之前，每个头的输出乘以 σ(gate + bias)，其中 gate 来自其自身的全宽投影，并带有一个学习到的逐头 bias。一个头可以逐 token 被调低或关闭。
Only the 9 full-attention layers keep KV for the whole sequence:
每个 token 有 9 × 2 × 8 × 128 个值，即 BF16 下 36 KiB，FP8 下 18 KiB。
在分片之前，完整 1M token 上下文约需 18 GiB 的 FP8 KV。

blocks.text: MoE 与残差流

inlines.text: 256 个路由专家（d_ff 2,560，NVFP4），路由方式与 DeepSeek-V3 相同：sigmoid 分数加校正 bias 从 8 个专家组中选出最好的 4 个，然后选出前 8 个专家，重新归一化后的权重再乘以 2.5。与 DeepSeek-V3 不同，这里没有共享专家。第 0–2 层改用稠密 SwiGLU MLP（d_ff 20,480）。
5120 × 256 的路由器权重、累加和 logits 全部为 FP32。
每个子层之前有一个 RMSNorm，之后还有一个。

blocks.text: SkyRL 团队使用 DAPO 配方对 Beam 模型进行了后训练，推理使用 vLLM，训练使用 Megatron。LoRA、全量微调和 MXFP8 RL 在 50 个训练步骤（即 100 次优化器更新，推理 minimal）中取得了相似的性能提升，在 AIME25 上的平均准确率（avg@8）从约 61% 跃升至约 79%。在 LoRA 和 BF16 全量微调启用 Rollout Routing Replay (R3) 的情况下，Megatron 与 vLLM 之间的平均绝对 log 概率差保持在 0.01 以下，MXFP8 RL 则保持在 0.03 以下。

Model architecture
Beam is a 52-layer MoE decoder with hidden size 5120. The MoE routing follows DeepSeek-V3. The main differences are in the attention layers and in how the residual stream is normalized.

blocks.text: Attention

inlines.text: 43 layers use sliding-window attention over the last 512 tokens, with RoPE. The other 9 (every sixth layer, plus the last) attend over the full context with
Without RoPE, attention flattens as the number of keys grows. SSMax scales each query by
is the 1-based position, so the softmax sharpens as the context grows.
48 query heads, 8 KV heads, head dim 128. Q and K are RMS-normalized per head before RoPE or SSMax.
, each head's output is multiplied by σ(gate + bias), where the gate comes from its own full-width projection with a learned per-head bias. A head can be turned down or off token by token.
Only the 9 full-attention layers keep KV for the whole sequence:
9 × 2 × 8 × 128 values per token, or 36 KiB in BF16 and 18 KiB in FP8.
About 18 GiB of FP8 KV for a full 1M-token context, before sharding.

blocks.text: MoE and residual stream

inlines.text: 256 routed experts (d_ff 2,560, NVFP4), routed the same way as DeepSeek-V3: sigmoid scores plus a correction bias pick the best 4 of 8 expert groups, then the top 8 experts, and the renormalized weights are scaled by 2.5. Unlike DeepSeek-V3, there is no shared expert. Layers 0–2 use a dense SwiGLU MLP (d_ff 20,480) instead.
The 5120 × 256 router weights, accumulation, and logits are all FP32.
Every sublayer has an RMSNorm before it and another after it.
. With unit-variance sublayer outputs, the residual stream keeps unit variance at every depth instead of growing with it.

blocks.text: Agent-driven optimization

Our initial version of implementation was an unoptimized, almost pure PyTorch version of the model. We then optimized it autonomously with coding agents: they profiled the model, wrote the kernels, and benchmarked each change. On TP8, the seven changes below brought batch-1 decode from 8.95 ms to 3.30 ms per step, and an 8 × 2K prefill from 328 ms to 176 ms.

(−40% decode). The post-norm, scaled residual add, and next pre-norm at each of the 104 sublayer boundaries now run as one Triton kernel, with FP32 math and the reference's BF16 rounding points.
Fused Q/K norm, RoPE/SSMax, and output gate.
Per-head Q/K RMSNorm and RoPE (or SSMax) run as one kernel, and the sigmoid gate as another.
Both TP all-reduces in each layer run inside the norm kernel, built on FlashInfer's multicast all-reduce. After the MoE, the same kernel also combines the top-8 expert outputs.
Specialized GEMM kernel for the FP32 router.
The router used to fall back to a generic path. vLLM's small-batch FP32 router kernel now supports Beam's 5120 × 256 shape, keeping FP32 weights, accumulation, and logits.
Merged QKV + gate projection with a low-latency GEMM.
The Q, K, V, and gate weights are packed into one matrix at load time, so the four projections run as one GEMM. For small batches it uses a low-latency CuTe DSL GEMM or FlashInfer's TinyGEMM.
The Q/K norm and RoPE kernel now also writes K and V into the KV cache, so there is no separate cache-write kernel.

DFlash2 speculative decoding

Beam ships with a DFlash2 draft head, which vLLM supports from day 0. Instead of drafting one token at a time, it predicts a whole block of tokens in a single forward pass from the target model's hidden states.

inlines.text: draft head, which vLLM supports from day 0. Instead of drafting one token at a time, it predicts a whole block of tokens in a single forward pass from the target model's hidden states.

5 sliding-window layers that read hidden states from 5 target layers and share the target's embedding and LM head. A grouped convolution and a small candidate selector restore some of the left-to-right dependency a parallel drafter loses.

, vLLM predicts how likely each draft token is to be accepted and verifies only the ones worth their cost, instead of a fixed number per step. DFlash2 has no confidence head, so the acceptance estimate comes from the drafter's own logits (see our
The drafter's convolution, norms, and KV writes are fused, and the whole draft step runs in a CUDA graph. FP8 KV cache works for the drafter too, with no change in acceptance.

Adaptive verification pays off under load. At concurrency 128 it raises output throughput by 10.8% and cuts p99 TPOT by 9%, while verifying fewer draft tokens per step, which lowers acceptance length slightly but saves more compute than it loses. At low concurrency, where extra draft tokens are nearly free, it is neutral.

The command at the top of this post is a good default: TP4 on a single GB300 node, with DFlash2 and FP8 KV cache. To enable adaptive verification, add "enable_adaptive_verification": true to the --speculative-config. Other optimizations above are on by default.

blocks.text: We also collaborated with the SkyRL team to enable Day 0 support for RL on Beam. LoRA, BF16 full fine-tuning and MXFP8 RL are supported out of the box, with an upgraded RL stack for the 500B scale.

inlines.text: We also collaborated with the SkyRL team to enable Day 0 support for RL on Beam. LoRA, BF16 full fine-tuning and MXFP8 RL are supported out of the box, with an upgraded RL stack for the 500B scale.

blocks.text: The SkyRL team post-trained the Beam model on the DAPO recipe with vLLM for inference and Megatron for training. LoRA, full fine-tuning and MXFP8 RL achieve similar gains in performance in 50 training steps, or 100 optimizer updates (reasoning minimal), with an average accuracy (avg@8) jump from ~61% to ~79% on AIME25. Average absolute log-probability difference between Megatron and vLLM stays under 0.01 with Rollout Routing Replay (R3) enabled for LoRA and BF16 full fine-tuning, and under 0.03 for MXFP8 RL.
